subject: Order form: invoicing cadence, min-commit allocation & tax responsibility
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid Health Procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: invoicing cadence, min-commit allocation & tax responsibility

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the draft order form. Procurement at Orchid reviewed the commercial appendix and we have three open items before we can route to finance:

1) Invoicing cadence: your team proposed quarterly invoices with monthly usage true‑ups. We prefer a monthly invoice for easier cashflow reconciliation.
2) Minimum commit allocation: Orchid will be purchasing a 1.2M annual commit but we need the breakdown per quarter (and whether you allow transfers across quarters).
3) Tax and VAT liability: need confirmation on which party is responsible for VAT/withholding; also asking for your local tax residency cert.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide monthly invoices and a quarter-to-quarter transfer exception? If possible please include a clean redline showing the changes (we circled the relevant sections).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight timeline this week.

Best,
Samira Khan
Head of Procurement | Orchid Health
[Attachment: Orchid_Order_Form_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence, min-commit allocation & tax responsibility

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (finance leads on invoicing cadence) and Kimberly (legal / tax ops) to propose concrete language.

Preliminary answers:
- Monthly invoices: we can support monthly invoicing with a small admin fee (0.5% of invoice) if Orchid requires consolidated monthly billing instead of quarterly. Ben, please confirm mechanics below.
- Min-commit allocation: Redwood typically honors intra-year transfers up to 20% of the quarterly target with prior notice; we can make this 25% for the initial year in the order form if that helps.
- Tax/VAT: Kimberly, can you confirm the clause and whether we can accept Orchid's VAT exemption certificate where applicable? We will also provide Redwood's tax residency letter.

I've attached a redline ready for your review. If these high-level fixes look acceptable I can push a new clean copy for signature.

Thanks — Karthik
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Orchid_Order_Form_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence, min-commit allocation & tax responsibility

Karthik / Samira — quick follow from finance ops.

1) Monthly invoicing mechanics: we can generate monthly invoices for the committed dollars (1/12 of the annual commit) and then true up monthly for overage/underruns. If Orchid prefers a single monthly invoice rather than separate committed + usage invoices, we can do that but it requires a one‑time billing setup fee of $1,500 to cover reconciliation work. I've added suggested wording in Exhibit A (see attached pricing sheet).

2) Quarterly transfers: we can permit transfers across quarters up to 25% for year one. Language we propose: "Customer may reallocate up to 25% of the quarterly committed units to any subsequent quarter with 15 days prior written notice; reallocation beyond 25% requires Redwood approval."

3) Tax / VAT: Redwood will generally invoice net of VAT; customer is responsible for local VAT where applicable unless Orchid provides a valid VAT exemption certificate and a completed W‑9 or W‑8 (for US tax residency). Kimberly, please confirm the exact wording for the tax appendix — if Orchid is EU‑based for VAT purposes we should include a clause for reverse‑charge where appropriate.

Samira — attaching ExhibitA_pricing_schedule.xlsx with the proposed monthly invoice example and the revised commitment allocation table. If that model works I can prepare a clean order form with the adjusted clauses and the $1,500 one‑time setup fee line item removed if Redwood handles reconciliation internally (happy to waive on first year).

—Ben
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ExhibitA_pricing_schedule.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form: invoicing cadence, min-commit allocation & tax responsibility

Hi all — Kimberly from Legal / Tax Ops here. Quick clarifications and proposed language for the order form: 

1) VAT / withholding: Proposed clause — "Unless Customer provides Redwood with a valid VAT exemption certificate and completed tax residency documentation, Customer is responsible for all applicable VAT, withholding taxes, and related filings. Redwood will state VAT separately on invoices where required."

2) Tax residency: Redwood will provide a standard tax residency letter within 48 business hours after countersignature. That should satisfy Orchid's treasury team.

3) Invoicing cadence and fees: We are willing to issue monthly invoices consolidated for committed + usage and will waive the one‑time reconciliation fee for the first contract year. Please note, switching to monthly invoices may change payment terms processing (Net 30 by default). If Orchid needs Net 45 that requires finance approval; Samira, can you confirm preferred net terms?

4) Commitment transfers: I endorse Ben's 25% reallocation for year one. Proposed wording included in attached redline.

Next steps: Karthik, Ben — if you approve the wording I'll assemble a clean order form for countersignature and include Redwood's tax residency letter and a DocuSign link. Samira — if Orchid can confirm preferred net terms (Net 30 vs Net 45) we can lock the final draft today.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel (Commercial) | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Orchid_Order_Form_v2_redline.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]
